subject: Hospitality
title: The Motel: Born on the Highway
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Motel: Born on the Highway usable.

hook.text: The word 'motel' was coined in 1925—a blend of 'motor' and 'hotel' for a new kind of traveler: the driver.

buildup.text: America's interstate highway system in the 1950s created millions of road trippers who needed cheap, easy overnight stops.

discovery.text: Motels replaced the front desk with a parking-lot-facing door. Pull up, check in, park at your room. Speed was the product.

twist.text: Holiday Inn, founded in 1952, standardized the motel experience. Same quality everywhere—no surprises, no disappointments.

climax.text: The motel democratized travel. For the first time, middle-class families could afford comfortable trips across America.

punchline.text: No lobby, no bellboy, just your car and a door. Travel for everyone.
